metadata.title: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: Both expand squared expressions involving reciprocal powers before evaluating a definite integral. The candidate practises the expansion and power-integration prerequisite; it does not contain the original cancellation between two integrals.
sharedKnowledge: Both expand squared expressions involving reciprocal powers before evaluating a definite integral. The candidate practises the expansion and power-integration prerequisite; it does not contain the original cancellation between two integrals.

matches.rationale: Both test a short supplied list of numerical inputs and select exactly those satisfying the premise while falsifying the conclusion. The candidate changes powers to divisibility and adds an inclusive-OR conclusion.
sharedKnowledge: Both test a short supplied list of numerical inputs and select exactly those satisfying the premise while falsifying the conclusion. The candidate changes powers to divisibility and adds an inclusive-OR conclusion.

matches.rationale: Both check the exact prime/divisor definition before accepting an implication about integers. The candidate practises distinguishing a composite witness, an ineligible nonprime input and a supporting example; it does not ask for the first line of a proof.
sharedKnowledge: Both check the exact prime/divisor definition before accepting an implication about integers. The candidate practises distinguishing a composite witness, an ineligible nonprime input and a supporting example; it does not ask for the first line of a proof.

matches.rationale: Both decide when equal-width opposite signed areas force a zero integral and interpret that as a sufficient condition. The candidate replaces the sine period with a stated opposite-height identity about the integration midpoint; it does not prove necessity.
sharedKnowledge: Both decide when equal-width opposite signed areas force a zero integral and interpret that as a sufficient condition. The candidate replaces the sine period with a stated opposite-height identity about the integration midpoint; it does not prove necessity.

matches.rationale: Both reverse a squared equation, restore the lost sign restriction and identify roots introduced by squaring. The candidate gives a radical equation and proposed roots rather than an exponential family.
sharedKnowledge: Both reverse a squared equation, restore the lost sign restriction and identify roots introduced by squaring. The candidate gives a radical equation and proposed roots rather than an exponential family.

matches.rationale: Both translate line coefficients into intercept/gradient sign information, prove one implication and construct a line disproving a stronger reverse claim. The fixed-point condition replaces the original free coefficient signs.
sharedKnowledge: Both translate line coefficients into intercept/gradient sign information, prove one implication and construct a line disproving a stronger reverse claim. The fixed-point condition replaces the original free coefficient signs.

matches.rationale: Both use an arithmetic progression’s middle or median as the average of its endpoints, then test a universal conclusion. The candidate adds integer/parity cases and does not use a pentagon angle sum.
sharedKnowledge: Both use an arithmetic progression’s middle or median as the average of its endpoints, then test a universal conclusion. The candidate adds integer/parity cases and does not use a pentagon angle sum.

matches.rationale: Both audit a line-by-line inequality proof when a squared expression is replaced by sign/interval conditions. The original lower bound is redundant; in the candidate the negative branch is genuinely lost. The student must determine which situation applies.
sharedKnowledge: Both audit a line-by-line inequality proof when a squared expression is replaced by sign/interval conditions. The original lower bound is redundant; in the candidate the negative branch is genuinely lost. The student must determine which situation applies.

matches.rationale: Both translate only-if/iff statements into arrows and compare them with contrapositives. The candidate uses these equivalences to enforce a sole-true-option condition rather than compare three forms with a given theorem.
sharedKnowledge: Both translate only-if/iff statements into arrows and compare them with contrapositives. The candidate uses these equivalences to enforce a sole-true-option condition rather than compare three forms with a given theorem.

matches.rationale: Both solve equations involving a cosine square or magnitude, retain both cosine signs, reject impossible levels and list roots on a stated closed interval. The candidate has a fixed equation and also asks for the sum of the roots.
sharedKnowledge: Both solve equations involving a cosine square or magnitude, retain both cosine signs, reject impossible levels and list roots on a stated closed interval. The candidate has a fixed equation and also asks for the sum of the roots.

matches.rationale: Both recover cosine signs from a squared condition and count distinct roots including closed interval endpoints. The candidate first solves a quadratic in the cosine square instead of separating a free parameter.
sharedKnowledge: Both recover cosine signs from a squared condition and count distinct roots including closed interval endpoints. The candidate first solves a quadratic in the cosine square instead of separating a free parameter.

matches.rationale: Both use containment of sets of allowed inputs to decide which statement guarantees another, and then count or eliminate linked truths. The candidate asks for a sole true option rather than a condition forcing exactly three others.
sharedKnowledge: Both use containment of sets of allowed inputs to decide which statement guarantees another, and then count or eliminate linked truths. The candidate asks for a sole true option rather than a condition forcing exactly three others.

matches.rationale: Both use the product −1 rule for perpendicular nonvertical gradients. The candidate practises deriving a new perpendicular gradient and line equation; it does not repeat the original cyclic three-slope invariant.
sharedKnowledge: Both use the product −1 rule for perpendicular nonvertical gradients. The candidate practises deriving a new perpendicular gradient and line equation; it does not repeat the original cyclic three-slope invariant.

matches.rationale: Both determine a first contribution and common ratio from the given structure, check convergence and evaluate an exact infinite geometric sum. The candidate infers a surd ratio from a fourth term rather than binary place-value blocks.
sharedKnowledge: Both determine a first contribution and common ratio from the given structure, check convergence and evaluate an exact infinite geometric sum. The candidate infers a surd ratio from a fourth term rather than binary place-value blocks.

matches.rationale: Both split a function into regions with explicit formulas and add definite integrals piece by piece. The candidate practises that integration step after deriving a modulus recurrence; it does not use a ceiling or a geometric sum.
sharedKnowledge: Both split a function into regions with explicit formulas and add definite integrals piece by piece. The candidate practises that integration step after deriving a modulus recurrence; it does not use a ceiling or a geometric sum.

matches.rationale: Both finish by summing a geometric list with the correct first term, ratio and term count. The candidate obtains the geometric coefficients from differentiation rather than rectangular areas under a step function.
sharedKnowledge: Both finish by summing a geometric list with the correct first term, ratio and term count. The candidate obtains the geometric coefficients from differentiation rather than rectangular areas under a step function.

matches.rationale: Both derive strict parameter conditions on real quadratic roots and verify a necessary-and-sufficient description including excluded equalities. The candidate constrains the separation instead of positivity of the substituted roots.
sharedKnowledge: Both derive strict parameter conditions on real quadratic roots and verify a necessary-and-sufficient description including excluded equalities. The candidate constrains the separation instead of positivity of the substituted roots.

matches.rationale: Both require a strictly positive quadratic discriminant and retain both parameter-sign branches before applying domain restrictions. The candidate presents the resulting region graphically and does not include the quartic substitution or positive-root filter.
sharedKnowledge: Both require a strictly positive quadratic discriminant and retain both parameter-sign branches before applying domain restrictions. The candidate presents the resulting region graphically and does not include the quartic substitution or positive-root filter.

matches.rationale: Both distinguish zeros of a polynomial from zeros of its derivative by constructing or analysing polynomial examples. The candidate tests existence and sufficiency rather than all comparisons of two distinct-root counts.
sharedKnowledge: Both distinguish zeros of a polynomial from zeros of its derivative by constructing or analysing polynomial examples. The candidate tests existence and sufficiency rather than all comparisons of two distinct-root counts.

matches.rationale: Both explicitly count real zeros of a polynomial and its derivative on example polynomials, retaining repeated-root versus distinct-root distinctions. The candidate compares exact counts through necessity/sufficiency instead of adding a factor x to the derivative.
sharedKnowledge: Both explicitly count real zeros of a polynomial and its derivative on example polynomials, retaining repeated-root versus distinct-root distinctions. The candidate compares exact counts through necessity/sufficiency instead of adding a factor x to the derivative.

matches.rationale: Both test universal statements linking polynomial heights, derivative signs and signed integrals. Subtraction of integrands and a shifted polynomial counterexample are needed; the candidate does not contain an absolute-value input.
sharedKnowledge: Both test universal statements linking polynomial heights, derivative signs and signed integrals. Subtraction of integrands and a shifted polynomial counterexample are needed; the candidate does not contain an absolute-value input.

matches.rationale: Both compare a signed integral with expressions involving a function square and require a whole-domain polynomial counterexample. The candidate uses odd cancellation under a size bound rather than reflection through an absolute-value input.
sharedKnowledge: Both compare a signed integral with expressions involving a function square and require a whole-domain polynomial counterexample. The candidate uses odd cancellation under a size bound rather than reflection through an absolute-value input.
